long_biography.plain_text:
Coumantaros entered the family businesses in 1984, beginning with Southern Star Shipping and later joining Flour Mills of Nigeria's board. His father, George S. Coumantaros, had created both companies, so John's career began within an established commercial platform. He progressed through Southern Star's leadership and became FMN chairman in 2014, assuming responsibility for businesses spanning maritime trade, food manufacturing and agriculture.

At FMN, Coumantaros supported the group's expansion from flour milling into a broader food and agro-allied enterprise. The family's Excelsior Shipping structure already controlled FMN and acquired the remaining public shares before the company's delisting. Coumantaros's interest runs indirectly through Excelsior, with the precise personal percentage undefined. His career combines family succession with active development of the inherited platform. The ownership route gives him an economic interest in the businesses, while factories, subsidiaries, inventories and shipping assets remain with their respective companies. His current leadership centers on FMN's food business, while Southern Star represents the maritime side of the platform he continues to operate.
